hypothesis.title: Radiomics-derived CT imaging signature predicts high-risk neuroblastoma patients
hypothesis.population: Patients diagnosed with neuroblastoma (typically children and adolescents)
hypothesis.intervention: Application of a radiomics-derived imaging signature extracted from CT scans
hypothesis.outcome: Accurate identification of high‑risk neuroblastoma status
hypothesis.clinical_context: Use of CT‑based radiomic analysis for risk stratification in neuroblastoma to guide treatment intensity

steps.name: Comprehensive Literature Review & Feasibility Assessment
steps.description: Gather existing evidence on CT‑based radiomics in neuroblastoma, identify prior imaging signatures, assess technical feasibility across participating centers, and define gaps that the current study will address.

steps.name: Define Study Objectives & Hypothesis
steps.description: Formally articulate the primary hypothesis: a pre‑defined radiomics‑derived CT signature can accurately identify high‑risk neuroblastoma patients. Specify secondary objectives such as correlation with overall survival, progression‑free survival, and comparison with current risk stratification methods.

steps.name: Develop Detailed Study Protocol
steps.description: Create a protocol that includes study design (multicenter retrospective‑prospective cohort), inclusion/exclusion criteria, sample size justification (power analysis targeting ≥85% power to detect an AUC increase from 0.70 to 0.85), imaging acquisition standards, radiomics pipeline, statistical analysis plan, and data management procedures.

steps.name: Obtain Regulatory & Ethics Approvals
steps.description: Submit the protocol to Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) at each participating site, secure informed‑consent templates (or waiver for retrospective data), and register the trial on ClinicalTrials.gov or an equivalent registry.

steps.name: Select and Qualify Participating Centers
steps.description: Identify pediatric oncology centers with high neuroblastoma case volumes and capable CT imaging infrastructure. Conduct site qualification visits to ensure compliance with imaging protocols, data security, and personnel training.

steps.name: Standardize CT Imaging Acquisition Parameters
steps.description: Define a harmonized CT protocol (e.g., scanner type, slice thickness ≥1 mm, tube voltage 120 kV, standardized contrast timing). Provide a detailed imaging manual and conduct phantom studies to verify inter‑scanner consistency.

steps.name: Develop Radiomics Extraction Pipeline
steps.description: Implement a reproducible pipeline using open‑source tools (e.g., PyRadiomics) with steps for tumor segmentation (manual or semi‑automatic), image pre‑processing (resampling, intensity normalization), feature extraction (first‑order, shape, texture), and feature harmonization (ComBat). Validate pipeline robustness on a pilot dataset.

steps.name: Training Cohort Assembly & Signature Derivation
steps.description: Collect retrospective CT scans and clinical data from ~200 patients (≈30% high‑risk) across sites. Perform tumor segmentation, extract radiomic features, and apply dimensionality reduction (e.g., LASSO, Elastic Net). Derive the predictive signature using machine‑learning classifiers (e.g., logistic regression, random forest) and optimize via cross‑validation.

steps.name: Internal Validation & Model Calibration
steps.description: Assess model performance on an internal hold‑out set (e.g., 20% of training data). Compute discrimination metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) and calibration plots. Refine the model if needed.

steps.name: Prospective Validation Cohort Enrollment
steps.description: Enroll a separate prospective cohort of ~150 newly diagnosed patients across the same centers. Apply the pre‑defined imaging protocol, segment tumors, extract features using the locked pipeline, and calculate the signature score without any retraining.

steps.name: Primary Statistical Analysis
steps.description: Compare the signature’s ability to predict high‑risk status (as defined by INRG or COG criteria) against the standard clinical risk model. Use ROC analysis, DeLong test for AUC comparison, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and decision‑curve analysis to evaluate clinical utility.

steps.name: Secondary & Exploratory Analyses
steps.description: Investigate associations between signature scores and survival outcomes (overall survival, event‑free survival) using Kaplan‑Meier curves and Cox regression. Explore whether the signature adds prognostic value beyond MYCN amplification, age, stage, and serum markers.

steps.name: Quality Assurance & Data Monitoring
steps.description: Implement centralized data monitoring for completeness, image quality, and segmentation reproducibility (inter‑observer ICC >0.80). Conduct periodic audits and interim analyses to ensure planned sample size and event rates are being met.

steps.name: Data Management & Confidentiality
steps.description: Store de‑identified imaging and clinical data in a secure, HIPAA‑compliant cloud repository. Establish a data‑sharing agreement and maintain a data‑dictionary for all variables.

steps.name: Manuscript Preparation & Dissemination
steps.description: Draft manuscripts detailing methodology, validation results, and clinical implications. Present findings at pediatric oncology and radiology conferences. Share the radiomics pipeline code and anonymized dataset (where permissible) to promote reproducibility.

steps.name: Regulatory Submission & Implementation Planning
steps.description: If the signature meets predefined performance thresholds (e.g., AUC ≥0.85, NRI >0.10), prepare a regulatory brief for FDA/EMA (as a diagnostic device) and develop a clinical implementation roadmap, including integration into radiology PACS and decision‑support tools.
